How the brain got so powerful

Thirteen chapters, from the first neurons to you, with narration.

0:00 / 3:07

Chapters

    Still argued

    • Cooking. Solid evidence of controlled fire goes back about a million years. Regular cooking may be much later, so how much it drove brain growth is disputed.
    • Gut for brain. The trade-off idea (Aiello and Wheeler) fits humans well. Comparisons across other mammals do not show a clean gut-versus-brain pattern.
    • The social brain. Group size tracks neocortex size in primates (Dunbar). In some analyses, diet predicts brain size about as well.
    • Fossil sizes. The volumes shown are rough species averages. Individuals overlap a lot, and Neanderthal brains were as large as ours or larger.
    • Size is a crude measure. Neuron count and wiring matter more than volume. The 86 billion figure comes from direct cell counts; synapse estimates vary widely.

    Dates are rounded. The timeline strip in the video uses a log scale, so each step to the right is a much shorter stretch of time.
